near_miss.why_not: Partner link rests only on a mis-mapping: αὔω/ἀΰω 'shout' is not *h2ews- 'draw water' (nor 'dawn'); Homeric contexts are battle-cries, nothing to do with the naming rite. The inherited naming phrase *h1nomn̥ dheh1- (ON 'nafn gefa' would be a renewal of the verb) has no partner in the bundle.

near_miss.lead: ON 'vatni ausa' ~ Gk 'ἀφύσσασθαι ὕδωρ' (draw water); vatn ~ ὕδωρ cognate, verb renewed
near_miss.why_not: ON is the ritual sprinkling of a newborn, Greek is sailors fetching water; ἀφύσσω is not a reflex of *h2ews-; 'draw water' is everyday language (Lat. aquam haurire would be the only true *h2ews- + water match and it is not anchored).

near_miss.lead: skaldic 'kvǫl þolir ... heitr ... sveiti' ~ Gk ἱδρώς/ἱδρώσει τελαμών (sweat; *telh2- in þola and τελαμών)
near_miss.why_not: sveiti ~ ἱδρώς is a genuine cognate but in unrelated contexts (love-pain kenning vs warrior's strap soaked in sweat); þola 'endure' and τελαμών 'strap' share only the root, not a collocation.

near_miss.lead: ON 'frost né vind ... fraus' ~ Lat. 'venti ... pruinae' (frost and wind, both cognate)
near_miss.why_not: A list of weather phenomena is generic; Lucretius is a physical catalogue, the saga a narrative of a cold night; no shared syntax or figure beyond co-occurrence.

near_miss.lead: ON 'myrkt af nótt' ~ Serb. 'мркла ноћ' / 'ноћи мрака' (dark night: myrkr ~ mrk-/mrak, nátt ~ noć)
near_miss.why_not: Both pairs cognate (myrkr ~ Slav. mrak- is a Gmc-BSl lexeme) and 'мркла ноћ' is a stock Vuk formula (22x), but ON uses an impersonal predicate ('it was dark from night', also 'náttmyrkr'), Serbian an attributive or genitive; 'dark night' is universal and myrkr is simply the ordinary ON word for darkness. Not defensible as inherited phraseology.

near_miss.lead: ON 'liggr ... sefr ... um nǽtr' ~ Russ. 'легъ спать на темную ночь' (lie, sleep, night all cognate)
near_miss.why_not: Three cognates but the collocation 'lie down to sleep at night' is everyday language; the byliny line is a late epic formula and the saga sentence is plain prose about someone's sleeping place.

near_miss.lead: ON 'mér sé ǫnnur móðir ... eða faðir' ~ Skt 'na me 'sti mātā na pitā' (dative possessor + be + mother/father)
near_miss.why_not: Kinship-term pairs and dative-of-possession are generic; contexts differ (refusing a foster-family vs an orphan's plea); ON order mother-father is not even a fixed binomial here.

near_miss.lead: ON 'um várit ... um sumarit' ~ AV season lists (vasanta ~ vár)
near_miss.why_not: Saga uses seasons as time adverbs; AV enumerates seasons ritually. No shared figure.

near_miss.lead: ON 'setr Steinvǫru í kné sér' ~ Skt 'jānuni āropya' (set on the knee)
near_miss.why_not: Tested against the knee-setting rite (ON knésetja, Od. 19 child on Autolykos's knees), but here Bersi just takes a girl onto his lap on horseback; Skt is breaking an enemy's back over the knee. Unrelated contexts.

near_miss.lead: ON 'um nóttina hvíldi' ~ Lat. 'noctu ... quietus' (*kʷyeh1- rest + night)
near_miss.why_not: hvíla ~ quies is cognate but 'rest at night' is generic; Plautus is comic complaint, saga is sleeping arrangements.

near_miss.lead: ON 'leggr hǫfuðit í kné henni ok sofnar' ~ Hitt. Tešimi asleep 'genuwaš' with the beloved (kné ~ genu-, sofna ~ šuppariya-)
near_miss.why_not: Closest lead in the set: cognate knee + sleep in an intimate setting (woman's lap; goddess asleep on the beloved's knees in the Nerik myth). But sleeping with one's head in a lover's lap is a universal gesture, the syntax differs (ON head laid in knee; Hitt. sleeping 'sweet sleeps' on the knees), and Edda 'í meyjar kné' (Þrymskviða, hammer in the bride's lap) points to a different lap symbolism. Not claimable.
Single cognate adjective, different referents (a foul thing said of a poet vs foul-smelling anger as a drink).

error.correct_reading: αὔω/ἀΰω 'shout, cry out' (cf. ἀϋτή 'battle-cry'), not a reflex of *h2ews-
error.evidence: Context 'αὖε δ' ἑταίρους' = 'called to his comrades'; the homograph αὔω 'kindle' is a different verb and neither is *h2ews- 'draw water'.

error.correct_reading: ἀΰω 'shout' aor. ἤϋσε, 'he shouted three times as loud as a man's head could hold'
error.evidence: Same mis-mapping; this partner was retrieved only through it.

error.correct_reading: ἀφύσσω 'draw (liquid)' has no accepted IE etymology; it cannot be a regular reflex of *h2ews- (which gives Lat. haurio, ON ausa)
error.evidence: Phonology: *h2ews- would give Gk αὑ-/αὐ-, not ἀ-φυσσ-.

error.correct_reading: eš- 'be', pret. 3 sg. ešta, with the participle šuppariyanza 'was asleep'
error.evidence: Periphrasis participle + ešta; 'sit' is middle (ešari/ešat), not ešta.
